answer: An agent economy can mitigate Sybil attacks through remote hardware attestation. To register, each node connects to an admission inlet where an enclave-bound asymmetric cipher signs its isolated runtime state. This forces an adversary to acquire scarce physical security chips rather than conjuring a sprawling plume of synthetic nodes on virtual machines. However, side-channel vulnerabilities in enclave silicon can occasionally allow attackers to extract signing keys and forge identities.
